Added two new Cache-Control header rules to vercel.json: /fonts/(.*) gets `public, max-age=31536000, immutable` (one font file, never content-modified in repo history — safe); /(.*)\.(js|css) gets `public, max-age=300, stale-while-revalidate=86400` instead of the naive immutable recipe — filenames (app.compiled.min.js, style.min.css, etc.) are unhashed and this loop merges to main (auto-deploying via Vercel) multiple times a day, so a 1-year immutable cache would risk serving stale/broken JS to repeat visitors for up to a year after any deploy; 5min-fresh + 1day-SWR gives most of the perf win (kills same-session re-fetch) while a deploy still reaches a returning visitor on their next request after one background refetch. `/` and `/home` (the sacred __APP_MODE router entry points) left untouched at max-age=0, must-revalidate. ROOT CAUSE: the subscription pick handler skips the amount step and seeds `capital = Math.ceil(foreverNumber(target, guidanceApy)/100)*100` at the conservative guidance rate (`guidanceApy = stableGuidanceApy || 5.5`, planner.js:3592/3863) ≈ $4,400-4,800; the bloom's headline (`subHeroWinCovers`) and forever/mix-total line (`mixTotal`) recompute coverage from `currentMixStats.neededCapital` at the LIVE blended apy (10.58% → ≈$2,300), but the checkout hero card reads `slideCapital` (via `chkBaseCapital`, planner.js:2628) which was still the stale seed; the `slideCapital`⇄`neededCapital` sync effect (planner.js:1529) had a `!mixTouched` early-return so it only realigned AFTER the user touched the mix — the untouched default state diverged (same class as 085's coveredBundle-default: a value seeded at one rate leaking onto a surface recomputed at another). FIX (single planner.js hunk): dropped the `!mixTouched` gate + `mixTouched` dep from the sync effect so `slideCapital` tracks the live-apy `neededCapital` from the initial seed on — one source of truth across the hero card, headline and forever line (and now refreshes on persona/APY change too, previously stale until the mix was touched). Chose the STATE-level sync over a `chkBaseCapital`-only patch deliberately: the plan strip (planner.js:2758) + make-it-yours summary (2828) also read `slideCapital`, so a hero-only patch would have left THOSE on the stale seed — syncing the state fixes every consumer at once and keeps the capital slider functional. Safe by construction: the amount step is skipped for subs so `capital` is always a seeded default (no user-typed value to clobber), and the effect is keyed on `neededCapital` not `slideCapital` so dragging the capital slider (an explicit override) never refires it. WHAT PRODUCTION DISPROVED: `/:path*` does NOT match the root path `/` on Vercel's edge. Cache was ruled out before concluding, which mattered because the alias root was serving `x-vercel-cache: HIT` with `age: 2878`: a cache-busted ROOT request still returned 200 while an equally uncached SUB-PATH returned 308 on the same host in the same second — same deployment, same predicate, only the path shape differs.

THE LESSON LANDED ON THE ITEM THAT WROTE IT: 211's own notes said the deploy is the only real gate, citing 212. It was. 22 offline assertions, 10 verifier-built mutants, and the verifier's own `path-to-regexp@6` walk — which matched `/` correctly in isolation — all agreed the config was right, and production disagreed. path-to-regexp matching `/` is not evidence that Vercel's edge does.

FIX: a root-only rule added as the new `redirects[0]` (`source: "/"`, same anchored host predicate, `destination: "https://www.defi.garden/"`, `permanent: true`), pushing the catch-all to `redirects[1]`. ADDITIVE ON PURPOSE — the tempting fix is swapping `/:path*` for the spec's original `/(.*)`+`$1`, rejected because `/:path*` is proven in production for every non-root path and replacing it would risk regressing working behaviour to fix a case a strictly-more-specific extra rule fixes with zero blast radius. `test_yield_garden_redirect.js` reworked for the two-entry shape (22 → 37 assertions): both entries asserted to carry the identical anchored predicate and `permanent: true`, the executed host match/no-match table runs against BOTH, the blast-radius scan permits exactly indices 0 and 1 and nothing else, and a new self-defeat case deletes the root rule and proves the count check goes red. The test header now records the production table so nobody merges the two rules back into one on the theory that a catch-all "obviously" covers the root.

ALSO OBSERVED, not a defect: `/plan.html` on the alias costs 2 hops (Vercel's generated `cleanUrls` redirect to `/plan` orders ahead of user redirects, then the host rule fires) — correct destination, within the spec's hop budget. The verifier predicted this exact ordering effect as residual 3.

Re-check `origin/main`'s BACKLOG for newly minted IDs before the first push, not only at pickup.**

**THE HEARTBEAT'S PRE-REGISTERED FIX LOST, ON MEASUREMENT.** Row 222 pre-registered "prefer REMOVING the duplicate render site (`app.js:3139`) — the sticky header already renders a working toggle" with a fallback if a surface depended on it. Measured on a real render: **the fallback was correct and the preferred option would have made things worse.** (1) The standalone `.theme-toggle`/`.language-toggle` pair is the **only** control on the analytics HOMEPAGE — `app.js:3001` gates the sticky header on a selected token/chain, so `.app:not(.has-results)` renders no header at all; deleting the render site strips that surface bare. (2) The header's OWN controls are **also unreachable** at 360/480px — not buried, **clipped**: `elementFromPoint → null` with `documentElement.scrollWidth === innerWidth`, so removing the duplicate would have left the user with ZERO working controls rather than one. Neither fact was in the row. The fix is therefore CSS-scoped, `app.js` has **zero diff**, and acceptance criterion 8 makes the homepage guarantee permanent instead of incidental.

**WHAT THE DEFECT ACTUALLY WAS** — measured on a fixture-routed render of `home.html?token=USDC`, at rest, EN and KO identical, before any edit: at 360×780 **FOUR** theme/language controls exist in the DOM and **none** can be pressed. Header `.google-control-btn.theme-toggle` `{x:562.8,y:31}` and `.language-toggle` `{x:498.8,y:24}` → `elementFromPoint === null` (centres past a 360px viewport, `scrollWidth` still 360 — clipped, not scrollable-to); standalone `.theme-toggle` `{x:284,y:32}` → hits `input.google-search-input`; standalone `.language-toggle` `{x:0,y:70}` → hits `button.google-nav-tab.active`. Identical at 480. At 768 the header's and the standalone `language-toggle` occupy the byte-identical rect `{x:500,y:20,w:48,h:48}`.

**THREE ROOT CAUSES, none an occlusion-clearance problem** — so `playbooks/fixed-overlay-occlusion.md`'s checklist did NOT resolve this one: (A) `.theme-toggle{position:fixed}` (`style.css:3913`) and `.language-toggle` (`:4029`) are UNSCOPED and the header's buttons carry BOTH class names (`app.js:3057/3062` render `className:'google-control-btn theme-toggle'`), so they were yanked out of the header's flow onto the standalone pair's coordinates — which is why `.google-header-controls` measured `w:0 h:0` at 768px; (B) `.google-header-content` (`:928`) has NO `@media` override anywhere in the file and its `flex:1` search container/input (`:952`,`:973`) lack `min-width:0`, so the row cannot shrink below the input's intrinsic ~170px and pushes its own controls off the right edge at ≤640px; (C) `.app:not(.has-results) .theme-toggle` (`:4329`) is the only rule restoring `position:fixed` at ≤640px and never matches a results page by construction. FIX reuses the header's existing `.google-control-btn` controls (2026-07-10 standing decision): scope the floating rules off them, `display:none` the standalone duplicates on `.app.has-results` only (child combinator — the header's buttons are GRANDchildren; a descendant selector would have hidden them too), let the header row shrink at ≤640px.

**THE ATTEMPT-1 FAIL IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING THIS ITEM PRODUCED.** Attempt 1 shipped those three blocks, passed **17/17** of its own rendered criteria, and was FAILED by the verifier for a defect none of its criteria could express: it had introduced a NEW P1 occlusion on its own target surface. `.app.has-results`'s mobile clearance is only `padding-top: var(--space-20)` (20px) against a 120-127px fixed header — arithmetic that should have buried `.results-title` all along. It didn't, because the two **broken** standalone buttons sat in flow above the content contributing ~92px of margin. **The clearance keeping the page readable was accidental, and supplied by the very defect being fixed.** `.container`'s top went `y:112` → `y:20`. The operator reproduced it independently against a true `git checkout f66ea3fde5 -- style.css style.min.css` baseline — and caught its own first attempt at that baseline being worthless (`git stash` on an already-clean tree silently measured the shipped tree twice; redone properly). Baseline vs attempt 1: `.results-title` `y:141.7` clear → `y:49.7` hitting `.google-header-content` at 360 and 480; `y:169.7` → `y:57.7` at 640; 768 already occluded on baseline; 1280 unaffected. The spec's own Territory note had said not to touch that `padding-top` — its stated premise ("the grid content below is measured clear") was true ONLY because of the toggles, so the note was explicitly SUPERSEDED in a written addendum rather than quietly ignored.

**ATTEMPT 2** — `.app.has-results{padding-top:140px}` at ≤768px, replacing the accidental clearance with a declared one. Sized from measurement, not taste: header heights 120px (EN)/123px (KO) at ≤640px, 124/127px at 700-768px, max **127**, with `.results-title` ~29.7px below `.container`'s top → ~169.7px, clearing by ~42px. The addendum PRE-REGISTERED a ≥135px floor and a ~160px stop-and-report ceiling so the number could not be fitted to whatever turned the suite green. Operator re-measured at 360/390/414/480/640/700/768 × EN/KO: `titleHit=true` at every one. It also clears the **pre-existing** 768px occlusion — disclosed, not carved out, since the same value fixes both.

**THE GATE**: `test_mobile_controls_reachable.js`, new, 628 lines, wired into `test:serial` — **28 assertions**, 11 criteria across 360/480/640/768/1280 × EN/KO × light/dark × `?token=`/`?chain=`, always at `scrollY === 0` (asserted, never scrolled). Criterion 2 is a HIT TEST not rect algebra (a rect can miss intersection by sub-pixel rounding while the overlay still steals the tap); criterion 4 uses a real Playwright `click()` which throws on interception; criterion 8 guards the scoping by asserting the analytics HOMEPAGE (`?app=1` — verified `app` is in `home.html:77`'s `ANALYTICS_PARAMS` and yields `.app:not(.has-results)`) keeps its standalone pair; criterion 11 asserts `.results-title`/`.results-header` clearance by rect AND hit test. THREE red proofs — two added because the verifier's finding 3 was that the original only exercised the ≥641px duplicate-paint signature and never the item's own P0: a 360px proof asserting the UNREACHABLE signature (`elementFromPoint → null` while `scrollWidth === innerWidth`), and a criterion-11 proof mutating `padding-top` back to 20px.
